title: A Protocol for the Ghost
premise: Tamsin Thackeray, a private security contractor who faked his own death three years ago to escape the covert network that trained him, receives a calendar invitation from Marcus Vale—the handler he watched die. The invitation is real, sent by someone inside the network who knows Tamsin is alive, and it's bait in a purge designed to erase every operative who could testify about the program's crimes. Forced out of hiding, Tamsin allies with a disgraced federal auditor and the dead handler's daughter to expose the network before its architect, Director Ilsa Renner, completes the cleanup. In the end, Tamsin trades his anonymity for justice: he surrenders the evidence and himself, choosing truth over the survival he built his whole life around.
about_author: Orsen Montrose is the pen name of a former risk consultant who spent a decade writing threat assessments for clients he was never allowed to name. He lives off-grid in coastal Maine, where he still keeps a go-bag by the door out of habit.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Tamsin Thackeray, working low-profile security in Lisbon under an assumed name, receives a calendar invite from Marcus Vale—his handler, dead for three years. POV: Tamsin. The beat is cold dread: the polished lie of his new life cracks open with a single notification.

chapters.title: Go-Bag Rules
chapters.summary: Tamsin runs his escape protocols, burning his apartment identity while interrogating how anyone found him. Flashbacks establish Vale as the man who trained him to vanish. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into paranoia.

chapters.title: The Auditor
chapters.summary: Federal auditor Dana Okafor, suspended for chasing a ghost program called LATTICE, traces the same anomaly that exposed Tamsin. She stakes out his safehouse. POV: Dana. Beat: stubborn curiosity curdling into fear when she realizes someone else is watching her too.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Window
chapters.summary: Tamsin decides to attend the meeting rather than run, reasoning that running confirms he's alive. He preps counter-surveillance. POV: Tamsin. Beat: grim resolve—he'd rather face the trap than live hunted forever.

chapters.title: Café Meridian
chapters.summary: The meeting is a dead drop, not a person: a drive containing Vale's contingency file naming six operatives marked for termination—including Tamsin. A watcher photographs him leaving. POV: Tamsin. Beat: the trap springs; invisibility is officially over.

chapters.title: Six Names
chapters.summary: The drive lists targets and a kill schedule beginning in nine days. Tamsin recognizes the tradecraft as LATTICE internal. POV: Tamsin. Beat: horror shifting to purpose—if they're hunting six, six can hunt back.

chapters.title: Renner
chapters.summary: Director Ilsa Renner reviews the Lisbon photograph and orders full asset recall. Her chapter reveals LATTICE's origin: deniable contractors for jobs governments couldn't touch. POV: Ilsa. Beat: chilling bureaucratic calm—she calls murder 'records management.'

chapters.title: Uneasy Alliance
chapters.summary: Dana confronts Tamsin at gunpoint; he convinces her the program she audited is real by showing her the kill list. They agree to work together uneasily. POV: alternating. Beat: distrust becoming fragile partnership.

chapters.title: Vale's Daughter
chapters.summary: In Berlin, Tamsin finds Lena Vale, who inherited her father's encrypted legacy and hates him for the lies. She has half a key. POV: Lena. Beat: resentment wrestling with the need to know what her father really was.

chapters.title: First Loss
chapters.summary: Operative Yusuf Adeyemi, target two on the list, is found dead in Nairobi before Tamsin can reach him—staged as suicide. POV: Tamsin. Beat: the race becomes real; the clock is bleeding.

chapters.title: The Cleaner
chapters.summary: Renner deploys Wren, LATTICE's best closer and Tamsin's former trainee partner, with standing orders. POV: Wren. Beat: professional detachment masking a flicker of doubt about the list.

chapters.title: Half a Key
chapters.summary: Lena decrypts her fragment: financial routing proving LATTICE was funded through defense appropriations—a congressional crime, not just a rogue op. POV: Lena. Beat: grief transmuted into fury.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Tamsin calculates odds: four targets left, eight days, one team. Dana argues for going legal; Tamsin argues the law moves slower than bullets. POV: Tamsin. Beat: loyalty vs. truth theme crystallizes between them.

chapters.title: Target Three
chapters.summary: They extract Marisol Ferreira, a retired LATTICE analyst, from Porto minutes before Wren's team hits. Marisol carries institutional memory—and a grudge. POV: Marisol. Beat: desperate relief shadowed by survivor's guilt.

chapters.title: What Marisol Knew
chapters.summary: Marisol reveals Operation HALLOWED GROUND, a civilian casualty event covered up by Renner—the crime Vale died trying to document. POV: Marisol. Beat: moral vertigo; the scale of the lie exceeds anything Tamsin imagined.

chapters.title: Wren Closes In
chapters.summary: Wren tracks the Porto extraction, finding Tamsin's signature tradecraft everywhere. She requests permission to take him alive. Renner refuses. POV: Wren. Beat: first open fracture of loyalty.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Tamsin's recruitment and training, Vale teaching him that survival requires no fixed address, no true name, no attachments. POV: Tamsin (past). Beat: understanding how thoroughly the network made him—and why he must unmake it.

chapters.title: Compromised Channel
chapters.summary: Dana's official channels are monitored; her suspension is upgraded to a warrant. The legal path closes. POV: Dana. Beat: disillusionment—justice inside the system may be a fiction too.

chapters.title: Lisbon Reversal
chapters.summary: Tamsin baits Wren with a false meet, buying time but burning a contact who pays with his life. POV: Tamsin. Beat: guilt—the price of survival is now being paid by others.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name
chapters.summary: Target four, cryptographer Anton Brandt, offers to trade full decryption keys for extraction—but only to Tamsin personally, whom he doesn't trust anyone else to send. POV: Anton. Beat: wary bargaining.

chapters.title: Vienna Handoff
chapters.summary: The handoff is ambushed by a second LATTICE cell; Brandt dies passing Tamsin the key. Wren arrives and, seeing the ambush wasn't hers, hesitates. POV: Tamsin. Beat: chaos, loss, and Wren's doubt made visible.

chapters.title: Two Ghosts
chapters.summary: Wren corners Tamsin alone; instead of shooting, she demands the truth about HALLOWED GROUND—he shows her Vale's file. POV: Wren. Beat: loyalty pivoting; she gives him a twelve-hour head start she'll have to answer for.

chapters.title: Renner's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilsa chapters deepen: flashbacks show her recruiting Vale, then ordering his death when he grew a conscience. She begins shredding the paper trail. POV: Ilsa. Beat: ambition revealed as fear—she's destroying evidence of her own signature decisions.

chapters.title: Assembly
chapters.summary: Tamsin, Dana, Lena, and Marisol consolidate in a farmhouse outside Graz, merging fragments into a complete case file. POV: ensemble via Tamsin. Beat: cautious hope—the truth finally has a shape.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Marisol's old emergency contact protocol betrays their location; she confesses she panicked and pinged the network. POV: Marisol. Beat: shame and the terrible arithmetic of trust.

chapters.title: Farmhouse Siege
chapters.summary: LATTICE assault teams hit the farm at dawn. The group scatters along planned escape routes; Marisol stays behind to hold the door and doesn't make it out. POV: Tamsin. Beat: sacrifice—another debt added to survival's bill.

chapters.title: Split Paths
chapters.summary: Dana insists on taking copies to a Senate contact; Tamsin argues the network owns too many doors. They split the evidence as insurance against each other's failure. POV: Dana. Beat: partnership tested by divergent definitions of justice.

chapters.title: Dana's Gauntlet
chapters.summary: Dana reaches Senator Hollis, who listens—then reveals he's been sitting on LATTICE knowledge for years, complicit through silence. He wavers. POV: Dana. Beat: outrage meeting the banality of institutional cowardice.

chapters.title: Hollis Decides
chapters.summary: Renner's people pressure Hollis; Dana forces his hand by threatening to go public without him. He agrees to a closed hearing—in seventy-two hours. POV: Dana. Beat: a hard-won inch of ground.

chapters.title: Twelve Hours Spent
chapters.summary: Wren is summoned to Renner, who knows she let Tamsin go. Offered redemption for killing him, Wren stalls, then vanishes—now a target herself. POV: Wren. Beat: defection completed; the hunter becomes the seventh name.

chapters.title: Vale's Last Message
chapters.summary: Lena's key unlocks Vale's final video: proof of HALLOWED GROUND orders signed by Renner, plus Vale's confession that he recruited Tamsin and always intended him to be the one who survived to testify. POV: Lena/Tamsin. Beat: devastating clarity—Tamsin's whole exile was Vale's design.

chapters.title: Betrayal's Shape
chapters.summary: Tamsin rages at being manipulated even by the man he mourned; Lena argues Vale gave him the only ending available: purpose. POV: Tamsin. Beat: anger resolving into acceptance—loyalty to the dead means finishing their work.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Renner captures Dana to force an evidence trade. Tamsin agrees to meet alone, planning double-blinds with Wren, who owes the network a debt of her own. POV: Tamsin. Beat: cold focus; the gambler's calm before ruin or win.

chapters.title: Rooftop Terms
chapters.summary: The exchange in Vienna goes sideways when Renner's second, Callum Reeve, tries to kill everyone including Wren. Tamsin saves Dana; Wren kills Reeve. POV: Wren. Beat: violent catharsis and irrevocable commitment.

chapters.title: Burning the Network
chapters.summary: With Wren's access codes, the team triggers LATTICE's own records-management protocol against itself, mirroring files to distributed servers and the hearing. Renner watches her archive copy itself into exposure. POV: Tamsin. Beat: triumphant inversion—the machine devours its keeper.

chapters.title: Renner's Endgame
chapters.summary: Cornered, Renner attempts to destroy the physical server farm and flee under diplomatic cover. Tamsin intercepts her convoy. POV: Ilsa. Beat: her composure finally cracking into naked survival instinct.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Crossing
chapters.summary: At the border crossing, Tamsin has Renner at gunpoint and every reason to pull the trigger—HALLOWED GROUND, Vale, Marisol. He chooses arrest and testimony instead. POV: Tamsin. Beat: the climax of character—justice chosen over vengeance, truth over the easy exit.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: The closed hearing goes public when Hollis, shamed by Tamsin's willingness to burn himself, opens the floor. Tamsin testifies under his real name, surrendering his false identities and accepting prosecution for his own past operations. POV: Tamsin. Beat: costly honesty—the price of survival, paid in full.

chapters.title: Sentences
chapters.summary: Renner and surviving LATTICE leadership are indicted; Tamsin serves eighteen months for his confessed crimes; Wren enters witness protection; Dana is reinstated. POV: Dana. Beat: bittersweet vindication—justice arrived, imperfect and late.

chapters.title: A Fixed Address
chapters.summary: Released, Tamsin visits Vale's grave with Lena, then unpacks—not just the go-bag, but the habit of running. He keeps the bag packed anyway, out of respect for who he was. POV: Tamsin. Beat: quiet resolution—a man who learned that staying visible was the only way to stay human.
